Roxygen

oopr-roxygen.Rmd

This package exports oopr_roclet(), which is designed to help document classes. To use additional roclets in a package workflow, refer to vignette("extending", "roxygen2").

Layout

The roclet generates documentation across three main components:

Constructor Method
Appears in the Usage and Arguments sections (if applicable).
Value Section
Features a described list of each class, including its member count and description.
Class Sections
Each class receives a dedicated section broken down into the following hierarchy
Overview
Both Description and Details subsections.
Members
A described list of all Fields and Methods, including their specifiers and descriptions.
Method Details
Each individual method breaks down into five subsections: Description, Usage, Arguments, Details, and Returns.

See the OoprVec() documentation page for a live example of this layout.

Usage

Classes

To document class-level @description and @details, use these tags directly above the class definition. As each class has its own section in a page, it is recommended to set page-level documentation via NULL.

## ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ##
#' @name example
#' @title example
#' @description
#' Page-level description
## ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ##
NULL

## ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ##
#' @rdname example
#' @description
#' Class-level description
#'
#' @details
#' Class-level details
## ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ##
oopr("example",, { })

Members

All public members must be documented, if not a warning is thrown. Documenting protected members is optional, and any documentation for private members is ignored.

Members will have their specifiers automatically added to the documentation, so users easily know if it is static, virtual, read-only, etc.

Fields

Fields (and properties) can be documented by using the @field tag directly above its definition:

oopr("example",,
{
  ## ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ##
  #' @field field `integer(1L)` \cr
  #'              A documented field
  ## ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ##
  field <- 1L;
})

Methods

Methods can be documented using the @description, @usage, @param, @details, and @return tags directly above the method definition.

oopr("example",,
{
  ## ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ##
  #' @description
  #' A documented method
  #'
  #' @param x `integer(1)` \cr
  #'          A documented argument
  #'
  #' @details
  #' Some details on this method
  #'
  #' @returns
  #' The return value of this method
  ## ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ##
  method <- \(x)
  {
    return(x + this$field);
  }
})

A warning will be thrown if @description, @returns or @param (for an argument, if any) are not provided.

Any tags used for the constructor method are automatically moved to the page-level sections. A constructor method does not have its own section like normal methods.

Re-use

To avoid repeating the same documentation across members, they can be re-used implicitly and explicitly.

Implicit

Missing tags trigger implicit documentation re-use based on two conditions:

Inherited Members
Automatically re-use documentation from the base class member.
Fields
Automatically re-use documentation from a constructor argument, if they share the same name

Explicit

Use the @inherit tag to pull the documentation of another class member (within from the same class or another). The expected syntax is @inherit class$member.

All inherited tags are copied over for methods, except those that are already in use. Allowing a choice over which parts of the inherited member to use.

.Rbuildignore

Generating documentation for internal classes can be helpful when using this package, given the auto-complete functionality with RStudio with the devtools::load_all() workflow. However, this generates a lot of help pages and aliases in the final package build which end-users do not need to see.

Any topic with an oopr class can use the @keywords .Rbuildignore tag to automatically add the .Rd file to .Rbuildignore.

Note that the actual .Rbuildignore needs to be amended alongside removing the tag if one decides to stop build ignoring a .Rd file.
